decisions.reason: Its adjustable quarter-pallet format fits the firm's cardboard display core and offers useful flexibility, so the option remains worth keeping open at relatively low cost.
The pegboard-back display is a distinctive and versatile retail solution within the firm's main competence, so there is still value in retaining it in the portfolio.

This generic quarter-pallet cardboard display overlaps strongly with other similar offers, and after several years the learning gained likely no longer justifies keeping a less differentiated option active.
The eighth-pallet format serves a somewhat different in-store use case and is inexpensive to maintain within a broad display range, so it is worth retaining for now.

A wooden display pallet sits less naturally with the firm's paper-based production focus and likely carries higher complexity, making abandonment more attractive once uncertainty has largely resolved.
A media-specific quarter-pallet display is both niche and exposed to weaker demand prospects for physical media, so management would likely reallocate resources away from it.
